newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Electricity Generating units plan new issues.
newsitem.headline: Thai Electricity Generating units plan new issues.

text.p: A subsidiary of Thailand's Electricity Generating Plc will raise 700 million baht ($22 million) through a new share issue, the firm said in a statement on Friday.

Egco Joint Investment and Development Co Ltd, a 99 percent owned subsidiary, would issue 70 million new shares at 10 baht per share to increase its registered capital to 800 million baht, the statement said. The company will ask for an initial 25 percent to be paid up.
Proceeds will support the transfer of shares of Amata-Egco Power Co from Egco which owns 30 percent of Amata-Egco and for other unspecified projects, the statement said.

Another subsidiary, Egco Mining Business Co Ltd, is set to raise registered capital to 200 million baht from 50 million baht by issuing 15 million new common shares. The initial pay up is 33 percent, the statement said.
The proceeds will be spent on operating mining projects, the firm said. Electricity Generating said it owns 40 percent of the company. ($1 = 32 baht)
